clue.text: Cheerful, though fired for pinching a card

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so the word for fired holds the card inside it

parts.note: a fire that is fired has been lighted
a heart is a playing card of the red suit

explanation.surface: Someone sacked for stealing a playing card is oddly cheerful about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests losing a job but means set alight; 'pinching' splits that word after its fifth letter to hold the card.
explanation.definitionFit: A carefree, happy person is said to be in good spirits, without worry.

clue.text: Insect's place on the way up

parts.note: locus is Latin for place, also used in English

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the street abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A bug's spot on a rising road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses ST to TS, added after LOCUS. The definition is printed with an apostrophe but stands for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are swarming grasshoppers, a type of insect.

clue.text: Fairy-tale servant with the light brown hair, say?

indicators.note: say suggests the girl's name is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair is a song by Stephen Foster

explanation.surface: A storybook servant described by her pale brown hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title 'Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair' (an American parlour song) supplies JEANIE, which 'say' turns into a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is the spirit of a lamp who grants wishes and serves its master in Aladdin.

clue.text: The stupidity associated with thieves

definitions.meaning: being thick means being dim, so this is dullness of mind
the idiom thick as thieves means very close friends

explanation.surface: Criminals are notoriously dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the phrase 'thick as thieves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimness of mind is one sense; the other is the closeness in the idiom about intimate allies being thick as thieves.

clue.text: At the end of the day it was uniform in quality

definitions.text: At the end of the day

explanation.surface: When all was said and done, the work was consistently good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' looks like a cliché but means literally evening, as in 'even' and 'evensong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic English uses the short form for evening, and level or regular work is described as consistent.

clue.text: Woman joins club for making furniture

parts.note: Rose is a woman's name
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A woman joins a club to learn cabinetmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is a golf club, a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a dark, fragrant hardwood prized by cabinetmakers.

clue.text: Rising river drowns frail leader of the little people

indicators.note: to drown something is to submerge it, so the river covers the leading letter
in a down clue, rising means the river name is read upwards

parts.note: the Nile is the African river

indicators.note: the leader of frail is its first letter

explanation.surface: A river in flood sweeps away the feeble chief of the fairies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses NILE to ELIN; 'drowns' puts F, the 'leader' of 'frail', inside it: EL-F-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes something pertaining to elves, the small folk of folklore.

clue.text: A future priest also found no way in at first

indicators.note: at first tells us the preceding pieces come before the word for also

parts.note: no can be zero, the letter O
Rd is short for road, a way
taken as written
and means also

explanation.surface: A trainee priest likewise found the road blocked when he began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is only a link; 'at first' puts the three short pieces ahead of the word for also. No as O (zero) is a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinand is a candidate for ordination, someone training to become a minister of the church.

clue.text: The importance of the Kensington area

definitions.text: The importance of the Kensington area

parts.words: The importance of the Kensington area
parts.note: reads as the status of a smart London district, but Kensington's postcode is W8, and that code spelt out in full is a word for significance

explanation.surface: Status attached to a smart part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington is a wealthy London district whose postcode is W8; the second definition is that code written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight means significance or influence, as when an opinion carries clout.

clue.text: At home in a French port, beginning to show worldly wisdom

indicators.note: the word in tells us the home word sits within the name of the port

parts.note: Cannes is a port on the French Riviera
someone at home is said to be in

indicators.note: the start of the word show gives just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Settling down in a Riviera town begins to show how sophisticated someone has become.
explanation.walkthrough: Cannes is a resort on the French Riviera, famous for its film festival; the home word sits after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Canniness is shrewdness, the practical good sense of someone who knows how things work.

clue.text: In the north a waterfall might!

definitions.meaning: in northern English dialect, from Norse foss, a cascade, as in place names of the Lake District
might as a noun means strength or power

explanation.surface: Seen in northern England, a waterfall might be impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' reads as a verb ending the sentence but is the noun meaning power. The waterfall sense is a northern English dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are real: a dialect word for a cascade in northern England, and a synonym for strength.

clue.text: An Arab chief, he, embraced by an Indian soldier

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the pronoun sits within the soldier word

parts.note: Sikhs were famed as soldiers in the Indian army
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arab leader is warmly hugged by a soldier from India.
explanation.walkthrough: Sikh regiments were a celebrated part of the British Indian Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikh is the leader of an Arab tribe, family or village.

clue.text: Girl overwhelmed by music, moving aimlessly

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being engulfed, so the girl's name goes inside the music

parts.note: swing is a jazz style of the big-band era
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl swept away by music drifts about without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Swanning about is British slang for idling showily, like a swan gliding.
explanation.definitionFit: To swan around is British informal for wandering about idly, without real purpose.

clue.text: Radial projection newly initiated, it's said

parts.note: a wheel's spoke is a rod radiating from the hub

indicators.note: initiated here means started, so only the opening letter of newly is used

explanation.surface: A newcomer is introduced to some radiating rod, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initiated' takes the first letter, N, of 'newly'. The definition reads as a phrase meaning oral or uttered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken is uttered aloud rather than written, which is what said describes.

clue.text: After a little cricket, players are gloomy

indicators.note: after tells us the players word follows the cricket word

parts.note: an over is a short unit of six balls in cricket
a cast is the group of actors in a play

explanation.surface: After a brief spell of cricket, the team look downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler, so 'a little cricket'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast describes a dull, cloudy sky, so dark and dreary.

clue.text: A painter left it around

indicators.note: the left word and it go around the painter, enclosing him

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
taken as written
RA means a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist abandoned something lying about the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a British painter elected to the Royal Academy. The whole clue also describes the answer: what a painter leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness on canvas is something an artist produces and leaves for posterity.

clue.text: Almost forced to include Jacob's brother in book

indicators.note: including something means taking it in, so the brother goes inside the shortened word
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: thrust means forced or pushed
Esau is Jacob's twin brother in Genesis

explanation.surface: A biblical sibling is nearly squeezed into a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final T; the brother then goes in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference volume listing synonyms.

clue.text: Dwarf digests parts of Times daily

indicators.note: to digest is to take in, so the dwarf holds the scrambled newspaper name

parts.note: Doc is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

indicators.note: parts of suggests the newspaper name is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A small man reads sections of this newspaper every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper, but is a British word for a cleaner. 'Parts of' rearranges the paper's name to MESTI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, the same as a domestic help.

clue.text: Urge to fight for media accommodation

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A call to arms over the journalists' seating.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'IS' in the held text is an OCR artefact; the page has no such word.
explanation.definitionFit: A press box is the reserved area for reporters at a sports ground or event.

clue.text: Go about selling goods? They say cyclists do it

indicators.note: they say signals that a word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: cyclists push the pedals, they pedal

explanation.surface: Selling things door to door is what bikers do, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' shows the cyclists' word sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to travel around selling wares, as a hawker does.

clue.text: Models made infrequently

indicators.note: made suggests the letters of models are made into something new

explanation.surface: Fashion models were rarely made, as if manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' rearranges MODELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, not often.

clue.text: Officer takes a pound from an American general

indicators.note: to take something from a word is to remove it

parts.note: George Marshall was a US general of World War II
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A soldier pockets money from a US general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes ... from' removes one L from MARSHALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a high-ranking officer, as in field marshal or air marshal.

clue.text: Many we induced to supply the plant

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held and printed as 'Many we induced to supply the plant (8)': the only reading is K (many) + WE inside DUCED, but no clue word gives DUCED; 'induced' would be insertion indicator and fodder at once.
annotationWithheld.clue: Many we induced to supply the plant

clue.text: Its fellows, we hear, may be involved in a revolution

definitions.text: Its fellows, we hear, may be involved in a revolution

parts.words: Its fellows, we hear, may be involved in a revolution
parts.note: fellows suggests comrades in an uprising, but heard aloud it is felloes, the curved rim segments of a ..., which turn round and round

explanation.surface: Comrades are said to be drawn into an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Felloes are the curved wooden pieces forming the rim of a cartwheel; they sound like 'fellows'. 'Revolution' is turning, not uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel's rim is built from felloes, and the whole thing rotates when the cart moves.

clue.text: One practising husbandry by distant foreign sea

parts.note: distant means far away
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: Someone farming beside a far-off overseas sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' signals a word from another language: French MER, sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is the work of raising crops and animals, the trade of a person who works the land.

clue.text: Married or single, adult is embraced by Aborigine

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside, so the adult letter sits within the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: Whether wed or not, a grown-up is hugged by a native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is embraced by' puts A after the M of M+OR+I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, its original inhabitants.

clue.text: Monster seen in centre of Korea around midnight

indicators.note: around has the middle of Korea surrounding the letter for midnight
the centre of Korea is its letters without the ends

parts.note: the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: A beast is spotted in central Korea at about midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' takes ORE from Korea; 'around' wraps it round G, the middle letter of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a fearsome creature.

clue.text: The thread of Mowgli's legendary life

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken out of the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A reference to the story of the jungle boy's fabled life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thread' looks like a storyline about Mowgli of The Jungle Book, but it is the cotton. The letters run across 'MowgLI'S LEgendary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton yarn used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: He's tight and more clumsy, the fly-by-night!

indicators.note: clumsy suggests the letters of the two words are awkwardly jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk man gets ever more clumsy, then slips away at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy' rearranges TIGHT and MORE. 'Fly-by-night' usually means a shady character but here is a literal night flier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger moth is a striped moth that flies after dark, so it literally flies by night.

clue.text: The plates get a hammering here in the kitchen

definitions.text: The plates get a hammering here in the kitchen

parts.words: The plates get a hammering here in the kitchen
parts.note: the surface pictures crockery being bashed by a cook, but the plates are metal bars struck with mallets, and the kitchen is orchestral slang for the percussion section

explanation.surface: Dishes are being banged about in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Orchestral players call the percussion section 'the kitchen'. The instrument is a set of tuned metal bars struck with small hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument's tuned steel bars are struck with mallets, and it sits among the percussion.
